title: Zheng Qinwen Makes History and Sings Karaoke After China Open Win
summary:
Tennis star Zheng Qinwen made history in Beijing by becoming the first Chinese woman to win the China Open. She beat Mirra Andreeva in straight sets, which means she won the match without losing a set.

The 24-year-old fell to the court after winning match point. Then, after her victory speech, she surprised the cheering home crowd by singing karaoke.

"The feeling was incredible. To win here in Beijing in front of my home crowd is one of my dreams," Zheng said. "I've been through a very, very tough year."

Zheng had elbow surgery last year and has struggled with her form and fitness over the past 12 months. Before this win, she had gone two years without a title. This was her first WTA 1000 title, one of the biggest kinds of tournaments in women's tennis, and the sixth title of her career.

Andreeva, who is 19, led early in both sets, but Zheng fought back each time. The second set was tied 4-4 before Zheng took control. The crowd was very excited and sometimes noisy between points. Zheng made a double fault near the end, but she stayed calm and finished the match with an ace, a serve her opponent could not touch.

"I felt like I just forgot how to compete after coming back from injury," Zheng told reporters. "Finally, after so many losses, I [found] my fire again."

It was her 14th career win over a player ranked in the top 10. Even after losing, Andreeva is expected to rise to number three in the world rankings. Zheng is set to jump 31 spots to number 23.

"I'm so hungry, honestly, for what's going to come next," Zheng said.
why_it_matters: Zheng's comeback shows how athletes can recover from injury and a tough year, and her win is a milestone for Chinese tennis.
